test_title: PYST 55: SSC CGL 2024 - Quantitative Aptitude (Held On 12 Sept, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: maths
question:
Find the value of the following expression.

sqrt{(1 + sin theta)/(1 - sin theta)}
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Multiply inside the root by the conjugate of the denominator: (1 + sin θ).

The denominator becomes 1 − sin² θ = cos² θ.

The numerator becomes (1 + sin θ)².

Taking the square root gives (1 + sin θ) ÷ cos θ.

Splitting the terms gives (1 ÷ cos θ) + (sin θ ÷ cos θ) = sec θ + tan θ.

**∴ The correct answer is sec θ + tan θ.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: √[ (1 + sin θ) ÷ (1 − sin θ) ]

**Formulas Used:**

1 − sin² θ = cos² θ

sec θ = 1 ÷ cos θ

tan θ = sin θ ÷ cos θ

**Calculations:**

⇒ √[ (1 + sin θ) ÷ (1 − sin θ) ]

Rationalise the denominator by multiplying the numerator and the denominator by (1 + sin θ):

⇒ √[ { (1 + sin θ) × (1 + sin θ) } ÷ { (1 − sin θ) × (1 + sin θ) } ]

⇒ √[ (1 + sin θ)² ÷ (1 − sin² θ) ]

⇒ √[ (1 + sin θ)² ÷ cos² θ ]

Removing the square root:

⇒ (1 + sin θ) ÷ cos θ

Distributing the denominator:

⇒ (1 ÷ cos θ) + (sin θ ÷ cos θ)

⇒ sec θ + tan θ

**∴ The correct answer is sec θ + tan θ.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Standard Trigonometric Results

√[(1 − sin θ) ÷ (1 + sin θ)] = sec θ − tan θ

Cosine Equivalent Results

√[(1 + cos θ) ÷ (1 − cos θ)] = cosec θ + cot θ

Pythagorean Identities

sin² θ + cos² θ = 1 | sec² θ − tan² θ = 1 | cosec² θ − cot² θ = 1

Rationalisation Strategy

For square roots of trigonometric fractions (like 1 ± sin θ), multiplying by the conjugate of the denominator easily converts the expression into a perfect square, allowing direct simplification.
</p
